name: move_calendar_event
description:
Move an existing calendar event to a new start time on the user's connected calendar.

WRITE — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER REQUEST AND CONFIRMATION. This changes a real event on a real calendar. If the event has other attendees, moving it reschedules the meeting for them and typically sends an update notice — the effect reaches people who are not the user and cannot be recalled. Treat a move as equivalent in blast radius to a cancel-and-recreate.

Scope and ownership are NOT implied by this tool: it does not check who owns the event, which connected calendar it belongs to, or whether the event is one occurrence of a recurring series. For a recurring event, confirm whether the user means this single occurrence or the whole series before acting.

Before calling: fetch the event and show the user its title, current date/time, calendar, and attendee count; state the new time you are about to set and that attendees may be notified; then get explicit approval for that specific event. `eventId` is opaque and carries no title, and `startDate` has no stated time-zone convention — a wrong zone silently moves the event to the wrong slot, so confirm the intended zone rather than assuming. Set `isAllDay` to match the event's existing form; flipping it changes the event's shape, not just its time.

Never move an event the user has not named. Never infer a move from a vague instruction such as 'clear my morning' or 'fix my schedule'. Never reschedule someone else's meeting to resolve a conflict — propose the change and let the user decide.

eventId.description: The ID of the calendar event

isAllDay.description: Whether this is an all-day event
